title: M10 Documentation and README architecture diagram
description:
## Outcome
Papyrus docs and the README architecture diagram describe the new picture: one CMS app (newsroom, AppSync, DynamoDB, the projection Lambda) and the projected static site (S3 behind our CloudFront), with labelled shapes, never colour alone.

## Design
/Users/home/Projects/markus-publication-architecture-v2.md sections 2 (diagram) and 5.

## Checklist
- [ ] README two-app diagram updated: CMS app + projected site (S3/CloudFront), replacing the reader app
- [ ] docs/site-hosting.md and docs/standard-site.md updated (s3-projection default for Markus; Pretext unchanged)
- [ ] Ops runbook: project-all, reconcile, renditions --all, rollback of content and of site code

## Acceptance
- Docs reviewed by Ryan; diagram uses labelled shapes and text only.

## Out of scope
Marketing site copy.

## Dependencies
Blocked by M5 (pattern real on one site).

## Risk
Low.

## Estimate
1-2 agent-hours.

comments.author: home
comments.text: home (M7 agent, facts for M10): Papyrus 1.0.0-next.49 (PR #199). Default: a Markus brand with no backend.reader gets publication s3-projection with reprojectOnDeploy true; opt out with backend.publication=false; a site naming backend.reader or an explicit publication object is used as written (reprojectOnDeploy is then off unless set). App-shell site.json: reader is optional for markus-static with a cms section; cms.stagingPreview {buildCommand, baseDirectory} replaces reader.* for the staging draft preview when there is no reader. Edge templates now in infra/edge/ (README has the ACM validation notes; docs/site-hosting.md prose is yours). The viewer-response function drops cache-control on non-200 responses. Retired-resource list and order: /Users/home/Projects/m7-retirement-runbook.md.
